signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options Skew + Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 163.68, maintaining a position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (162.41/161.05/157.71). COT JPY LF net short -114,030 confirms a crowded institutional carry trade, while retail sentiment is 85% short, creating a rare alignment where retail is fading the move alongside a strong institutional options hedge. The 25d risk reversal at -1.54 reflects the strongest put skew in the G10, signaling that despite the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage, the options market is paying a high premium for JPY protection ahead of the July 31 BoJ meeting. This combination of extreme short positioning and defensive options pricing makes the pair highly sensitive to intervention headlines or a hawkish BoJ surprise. Risk: BoJ holds and signals no further hikes, triggering a fresh round of carry-trade chasing toward 165.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Divergence + Vol Risk Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD is testing 0.6993, supported by a -71bp OIS carry advantage for the AUD (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%). While the RBA is on hold, the market prices a hike bias for the next meeting on 11 August, contrasting with the Fed's neutral stance. Volatility pricing shows extreme caution; AUD/USD IV at 13.2% vs HV30 at 6.0% creates a +7.2% Vol Risk Premium, the second highest in the G10. This indicates the market is paying for protection against a breakout despite price holding below its SMA50 at 0.7027. Bullish spec positioning (COT LF net +20,521) aligns with the carry advantage, but the high VRP suggests a lack of conviction in chasing the current level. Risk: RBA Governor Bullock's upcoming speech shifts the hike bias to a hold, triggering an AUD unwind.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5777, positioned above its SMA20 of 0.5759 but below the SMA50/200 levels. A sharp divergence exists between sentiment and data; COT LF net short is -31,649 (extreme long% at only 12%), while the NZD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) is at +22.2, a strong positive reading. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. If the RBNZ maintains its hawkishness at the 2 September meeting, this crowded spec short faces significant covering risk. Risk: Continued USD strength on safe-haven flows targets a break below the SMA20 at 0.5759, validating the short positioning.

signals.title: USD/CAD — WTI Correlation Break + Positioning
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4118, holding below its SMA20 (1.4131) following a sharp -8.29% drop in WTI oil prices to $81.9. The intraday correlation between USD/CAD and WTI has moved to -0.919, a deviation of z=-1.52σ from the historical norm, as CAD fails to weaken as much as the oil move would typically dictate. This resilience is occurring despite a heavy COT LF net short of -99,823 in CAD, suggesting that speculators are already maxed out on the CAD-short trade. The 150bp Fed-BoC carry advantage favors the USD, but the lack of CAD follow-through on the oil crash hints at positioning exhaustion. Risk: A rebound in oil prices triggers a short-squeeze in CAD toward the 1.4020 SMA50 support level.
